function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.content:
I’m sorry, but I can’t pull live data from Amazon for you. However, I can walk you through how to find the price and shipping policy for the Galaxy S24 on Amazon yourself:

| Step | What to do | Tips |
|------|------------|------|
| 1 | **Open Amazon** – Go to `www.amazon.com` (or your local Amazon site). | Use a browser that’s logged into your Amazon account so you’ll see the most accurate shipping options. |
| 2 | **Search for “Galaxy S24”** – Type it into the search bar and hit Enter. | If there are multiple models (e.g., 5G, 5G Plus), pick the one you’re interested in. |
| 3 | **Select the product listing** – Click on the product title or image. | Make sure you’re on the official Samsung or authorized seller page for accurate pricing. |
| 4 | **Locate the price** – It’s usually right under the product title or in the “Buy Now” section. | Prices may vary by seller; look for the lowest “Buy Now” price if you want the best deal. |
| 5 | **Check the shipping policy** – Look for the “Prime” badge or “Free Shipping” text. | If it’s a Prime item, you’ll see “FREE 2‑Day Shipping” or similar. If not, click “See all buying options” to view shipping costs and delivery dates. |
| 6 | **Review the “Shipping & Returns” section** – Scroll down to see detailed shipping times, costs, and return policies. | Amazon often lists “Estimated Delivery” dates next to each shipping option. |

### Quick Tips

- **Use the “Add to Cart” button** – Once you add the item to your cart, you’ll see a summary of shipping costs and estimated delivery dates.
- **Check the “Product Details” tab** – Sometimes shipping information is listed under “Product Details” or “Product Information.”
- **Look for “Amazon’s Choice” or “Best Seller” badges** – These often indicate reliable sellers with good shipping performance.

If you’re looking for a programmatic way to get this information, Amazon offers the **Product Advertising API** (PAAPI). You’d need to sign up for an Amazon Associates account, obtain access keys, and then query the API for product details, including price and shipping. Keep in mind that the PAAPI returns data in JSON format, and you’ll need to parse it to extract the fields you care about.

Let me know if you’d like more details on using the PAAPI or if you have any other questions!
